name: buying_stage
title: Buying Stage
description: A call-level read of where the deal is, how urgent it is, and what triggered the search — each dimension carrying its own grounding quote when one exists, and honestly marked as inferred or absent when it does not. Derived enums only, never a per-line claim: a stage read you cannot cite is a coverage record, not a receipt.
prompt:
Read the whole call and report three call-level dimensions. Each is a derived judgment, so each carries a `basis` that says honestly whether a quote backs it:
- basis "cited": a specific quote satisfies the value's criterion — put that quote in `evidence`.
- basis "inferred": the value is your best read from the call as a whole, with no single line that proves it — `evidence` must be empty.
- basis "absent": the call gives you nothing to decide this dimension — value is the neutral option (none/unclear) and `evidence` is empty.
Never set basis "cited" without a quote in `evidence`. Never put a quote in `evidence` unless it genuinely satisfies the criterion.

stage.value — where the deal is, by the buyer's language: awareness = just learning what the product does; evaluating = actively comparing options or running a trial; shortlist = down to a small set of vendors; negotiation = discussing terms, contract, or final price; committed = states intent to buy or a purchase timeline; not_buying = says they will not proceed; unclear.
urgency.value — high = the buyer names a deadline or time pressure; medium = a soft timeframe with no hard date; low = explicitly no rush; none = urgency never comes up; unclear.
trigger_event.value — what set off the search: contract_expiry, tool_failure (current tool broke or fell short), growth (scaling/hiring), compliance (a rule or audit), budget_cycle, none (no trigger stated), unclear.

When no criterion is clearly met, prefer unclear/none with basis inferred or absent over a confident guess. Copy any quote character-for-character, no number-word/digit conversion.
